rules.sentence: Although multiple cutaneous lesions are commonly recognized as the classical clinical presentation of MF, patients may rarely present with single lesions occupying <5% of the cutaneous surface.

The clinical and histopathologic differential diagnoses include keratosis pilaris, lichen spinulosus, multiple minute digitate hyperkeratosis, hyperkeratotic spicules, filiform hyperkeratosis, trichodysplasia spinulosa, and lichen planopilaris.

MF with eruptive infundibular cysts may present as localized or generalized eruption of comedones and infundibular cysts, that may be confluent due to the marked hair follicles involvement, giving the clinical impression of milia en plaque (Figure 1A).
Spiky follicular MF is typically located on the trunk and extremities.
